subject: Audit Trail Transfer & Retention Assurance — clarifications for HarvestBank RFP
messages:
From: Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@harvestbank.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@harvestbank.com>
Date: 2027-11-21T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on audit trail transfer and tamper evidence (RFP section 4)

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. A couple of clarifications from our compliance team on Section 4 (audit trail exportability and retention):

1) Immutability proof: we need assurance that exported audit records include tamper-evidence (signed manifests / checksums) and an explanation of how Redwood guarantees immutability when data is handed off to customer storage. Is a signed, timestamped manifest produced for each bulk export?

2) Chain-of-custody: does Redwood produce a verifiable chain-of-custody for snapshots (who accessed the data, when, and the transfer hash)? Our legal team expects an automated manifest that we can store with our evidence package.

3) Retention & WORM: we have a 7-year retention requirement in our contract. Can Redwood support a WORM-style retention export or attestations that records were retained and not altered in that window?

4) Export formats & sampling: preferred deliverable is compressed NDJSON with per-record metadata. We also sometimes request randomized sampling (5% stratified by region/time window). Can you describe sampling options and whether you can provide export previews before full harvests?

5) Timeline & cost: for a ~4 TB audit-line extract spanning two years, what typical turnaround and cost ballpark should we plan for?

I've attached Section-4 of our RFP. Please reply with short, concrete answers (we're consolidating for procurement).

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Grant
Senior Compliance Manager — HarvestBank
Attachments: HarvestBank_RFP_Section-4.pdf
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Questions on audit trail transfer and tamper evidence (RFP section 4)

Hi Sophie — thanks for the detailed list. Below are concise answers you can drop into your table. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you prefer.

1) Immutability proof: yes. Every bulk export produces a signed export manifest (JSON) containing per-file SHA-256 checksums, export UUID, and server-side timestamp. Manifests are signed with Redwood's key and include a signed HMAC we rotate quarterly. Customers can also request a detached PGP signature.

2) Chain-of-custody: automated. For each export we log: export initiator (user/service account), export job id, source shard ids, start/end timestamps, and transfer completion events. Those audit events are included in the manifest and are preserved with the export bundle. We can optionally include an access log slice showing which internal operators viewed the job details.

3) Retention & WORM-style attestations: Redwood supports export generation for WORM-friendly storage (S3 Object Lock compliant manifests and guidance). We do not enforce customer-side WORM after handoff, but we provide signed manifests and a notarized timestamp (RFC 3161 style) for retention attestations. For contractually required retention proofs (7 years), we can commit to retaining a signed manifest and a hashed index for the retention window; please let us know whether you need Redwood to hold copies under escrow or if you will accept manifests + hash lists.

4) Export formats & sampling: default export format is compressed NDJSON with record-level metadata (event_id, event_time, model_version, route, tokenized_length). Sampling options: deterministic stratified sampling (by time-zone, model route, or account), randomized seeds (reproducible), and pre-export preview (first 10k lines) on request. We support filtering by sequence-range and can produce both full and delta extracts.

5) Timeline & cost: for a 4 TB two-year extract we typically deliver within 7–10 business days for standard priority (includes QA manifest generation). Expedited (3 business days) is possible for an extra fee. Ballpark cost: $6k–$12k for the one-time bulk job (depends on redaction needs and retention packaging).

Next steps: I attached a short export-spec that maps fields and sample manifest (redwood-export-spec.pdf). If Legal needs stronger escrow or notarization terms we'll loop in solutions engineering.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on audit trail transfer and tamper evidence (RFP section 4)

Sophie — quick note from the account side: for customers with regulated obligations we recommend the following options (choose one or combine):

- Private deployment (Redwood Private) with customer-managed KMS: provides zero-trust export controls and retention enforcement prior to handoff.
- Escrow snapshot: Redwood can produce escrowed immutable snapshots (we hold a sealed copy under a signed SLA) for critical windows.
- Canary export: deliver a 50 GB pilot bundle first (manifest + signed hash); acceptance sign-off triggers the full harvest.

If HarvestBank prefers Redwood to maintain a sealed retention copy, we'll need to add that as an optional line item to the SOW.

Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Ben / Marissa — thanks for the fast responses. A couple of clarifications before we finalize procurement language: 1) For the 7-year retention ask, can Redwood confirm whether you will provide a notarized timestamp (RFC 3161) for each export manifest or only on request (additional cost)? 2) For WORM: we need an attestation that export manifests can be stored in S3 with Object Lock and a recommended configuration doc.

If you can confirm the notarization policy and share the S3 configuration guidance, we can update Section 4 and move to contract redlines.

— LegalOps (on behalf of HarvestBank)

On Tue, 23 Nov 2027 15:04:00 -0800 LegalOps wrote:
> Ben / Marissa — thanks for the fast responses. A couple of clarifications before we finalize procurement language: 1) For the 7-year retention ask, can Redwood confirm whether you will provide a notarized timestamp (RFC 3161) for each export manifest or only on request (additional cost)? 2) For WORM: we need an attestation that export manifests can be stored in S3 with Object Lock and a recommended configuration doc.

LegalOps — short answers: 
1) Notarization: available on request as an add-on; standard export manifest includes Redwood-signed HMAC + timestamp. RFC 3161 notarization is a billable service (we can include it in the SOW or as a post-delivery attestation). Typical lead time for notarized batches is +2 business days.

2) S3/WORM guidance: yes — we'll provide an S3 Object Lock configuration checklist and a sample lifecycle policy that maps to your 7-year window. I shared a Draft guide in our internal drive (link below) and will export a sanitized copy for your procurement pack.

Link to guide (sanitized): https://redwood-drive.internal/docs/exports/redwood-export-spec.pdf

If that works, I'll propose language for the SOW: (a) Redwood will produce signed manifests for every export, (b) notarization available per-batch as add-on, (c) Redwood will provide an S3 Object Lock configuration document and sample inventory.

I'll send contract-ready wording once I hear back.

Ben

I'll circulate an internal acceptance and ask Legal to prepare redlines.

Regards,
